PADLAB GUIDE · XBOX

Xbox Controller Test: Xbox One & Series Buttons, Sticks

By PadLab · Updated October 9, 2026

PadLab gives Xbox One, Xbox Series and compatible PC gamepads a fast browser-based input check. It reads the standard mapping when the browser provides one and shows raw values when it does not.

Start controller test →

Test an Xbox controller online

  1. Connect with a data-capable USB cable or Bluetooth.
  2. Open the controller workspace and press any button.
  3. Work through A, B, X, Y, the D-pad, View, Menu, bumpers and stick clicks.
  4. Press LT and RT gradually, then release both thumbsticks and run the drift sample.

What the standard mapping means

Standard browser mapping places A/B/X/Y at buttons 0–3, bumpers at 4–5, triggers at 6–7, and left/right sticks on axes 0–3. If the browser does not provide a standard mapping, use numbered raw inputs instead of assuming Xbox labels.

Check triggers and rumble

An analog trigger generally moves through values between 0 and 1. Some modes expose only digital states. Vibration appears only when the browser exposes a compatible actuator.

Read the button and trigger test routine.

Xbox controller not detected

Charging-only cables provide power without data. Try a second cable and direct USB port, then press a controller button while PadLab is focused. For Bluetooth, confirm it is not reconnecting to a console or another computer.

Choose the connection your model supports

Xbox controller models do not all offer the same wireless options. Check the exact model before troubleshooting Bluetooth. Use a data-capable USB connection as a comparison where supported; a charging light alone does not establish input connectivity.

Compare a direct controller with a virtual one

If the selector lists more than one device, press a button and identify which entry responds. Remapping software can expose a virtual controller alongside the physical device. Record its browser-reported name, then compare with the remapper closed when practical. Change one variable per test.

ObservationNext useful check
Buttons work, but a game ignores themCheck that game’s selected device and bindings.
One trigger stays above zeroRelease it fully, repeat the reading and compare another application.
Two device entries respond togetherCheck for virtual-controller or remapping software.
No entries appearFollow the connection and browser detection guide.

Troubleshoot detection or learn how Windows input modes differ from browser mapping. A blank browser mapping does not, by itself, prove that the device is using DirectInput.

Record a repeatable result

Test one control at a time, reset session coverage between controllers, and export the result after a drift sample. Record the model, browser version, operating system and connection separately. A green observed-button mark means a press was seen during this session; it is not a durability certificate.
